summary: Elevated TTFB for chat completions after runtime v2.4.0 / model onboarding
description:
Issue summary:
Elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) observed for chat completion requests starting shortly after a staged rollout of serving runtime v2.4.0 and onboarding of redwood-chat-7b-q4_0 to the model catalog.

Impact:
- Enterprise customer Acme Payments experiencing increased TTFB leading to client-side timeouts on interactive chat UI (5-10% of sessions).
- Increased 95th percentile TTFB from ~120ms to ~650ms for streaming chat endpoints in us-east.
- Affects hosted customers and some dedicated clusters with the new runtime.

Environment:
- prod - us-east (primary), some signals in us-west.
- Runtime v2.4.0 deployed to canary and 30% of host fleet on 2026-03-01 03:12 UTC.
- Model variants: redwood-chat-3b-v1.2 (server-side pinned), redwood-chat-7b-q4_0 rolled as compatible fallback.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use chat completions endpoint with conversation history ~1k-2k tokens.
2) Send streaming request with max_tokens=512 and temperature=0.7.
3) Observe time between request accepted and first token chunk (TTFB).

Observed behavior:
- TTFB increased to 300-800ms for affected requests; timeouts at customer side after 1s for some SDKs.
- No corresponding increase in per-token generation latency once streaming starts.

Expected behavior:
- TTFB should remain ~= 80-200ms for similar requests and contexts.

Logs/metrics:
- Grafana: /dashboards/ttfb/hosted shows 95th p90/p95 spike aligned to 2026-03-01 03:12 UTC.
- SRE traces show increased blocking time in kernel-selection and model-metadata loader during first-token path.
- pprof from a sample host shows synchronous disk read at model load path (~120ms) after runtime v2.4.0.

Additional notes:
- Customer ticket opened via Support (Acme contact: jessica@acmepayments.com).
- Customer experiencing user-visible timeouts and raised priority due to revenue impact for interactive payment flows.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Priya Kapoor (Support): Opened ticket after customer reported intermittent streaming timeouts and higher TTFB. Collected request IDs and example traces. Added to monitoring watches.

2026-03-02 - SRE (Marta Liu): Confirmed p95 TTFB jump in us-east starting 2026-03-01 03:12 UTC. Noted runtime v2.4.0 rollout and recent model onboardings. Initial hypothesis: kernel selection sync path introduced blocking I/O.

2026-03-03 - Eng (Ethan Morales): Pulled flamegraphs from affected hosts; found model-metadata loader performing synchronous lookup to /var/model-cache/manifest which added ~100-200ms on cold requests. Opening hotfix PR to defer metadata read to async path. Linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123

2026-03-03 - Support (Priya Kapoor): Informed customer of ongoing investigation and provided temporary SDK-level retry guidance and a suggested client timeout increase to 2s as a short-term workaround.

2026-03-04 - Eng (Ethan Morales): Deployed hotfix (PR #5123) to affected canary hosts, confirmed reduction in TTFB spike. Preparing coordinated rollback for clusters still on v2.4.0 where hotfix cannot be applied immediately.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-01 03:12 UTC: runtime v2.4.0 rollout begins (canary -> 30%).
- 2026-03-01 03:15 UTC: first observable p95 TTFB increase in canary; by 03:40 impact visible in 30% population.
- Profiling indicates blocking metadata read in model load path added in runtime change that attempted to validate quantization metadata synchronously.
- The new model redwood-chat-7b-q4_0 has a slightly different metadata layout exposing the codepath more frequently.
- Evidence: pprof / flamegraphs, Grafana alerts, and host logs (/var/log/redwood/serving.log) with repeated "manifest read" entries.
Hypotheses considered:
1) Runtime v2.4.0 kernel selection path introduced a synchronous file read for quantization metadata -> confirmed by traces.
2) KV cache warmup causing first-token stall -> partially contributes but not the primary cause.
3) Network/NFS latency for model cache -> investigated, not correlated across hosts.
Actions taken:
- Reproduced locally with synthetic load and long context; reproduced p95 regression.
- Created hotfix PR to make metadata read async and to add a short-lived in-memory cache during startup (PR #5123).
- Deployed hotfix to canary; observed p95 improvement from ~650ms to ~140ms for canary hosts.
- Scheduled rollback plan for clusters that cannot receive hotfix immediately.
resolution:
Workaround and mitigation:
- Short-term: increased client-side timeout recommendation to 2s and SDK retry guidance shared with customer.
- Immediate fix: rolled hotfix (PR #5123) to canary and targeted affected clusters; p95 TTFB returned to expected ranges on patched hosts.
- Rollback: for clusters that remain on v2.4.0 without the hotfix applied, coordinated rollback to v2.3.8 started 2026-03-04 11:00 UTC.
Follow-up actions:
- Create automated regression test that exercises model metadata path and measures TTFB for streaming endpoints.
- Add rollout gating to detect TTFB regressions during canary at 10% and block further rollout if p95 increases by >2x.
- Postmortem to be drafted and linked to INC-20260301-07.
Status: Partial resolution; hotfix deployed to majority of affected hosts, rollback in progress for remaining clusters. Will update when all customer clusters confirmed healthy.
next_steps:
1) Complete rollback for remaining clusters by 2026-03-05.
2) Monitor customer-specific telemetry for 72 hours post-fix and confirm no regressions.
3) Draft postmortem and share with customer and PS team.
4) Add unit/integration tests for model metadata loading and add canary TTFB gating.
resolution_status: In Progress - hotfix deployed to canary; rollback underway for remaining clusters
